slides.label: The hook
slides.source_text: The hook You type one line. It does the rest. you › "the invoice test is failing — fix it" …then, with no further input, the AI on its own: ✓ ran the tests saw it expected 121, got 100 ✓ opened invoice.py spotted VAT was never applied ✓ edited the code added the 21% VAT line ✓ ran the tests again PASS ✓ Illustrative trace: a passing test is evidence for that case. Review the diff and relevant edge cases before accepting the change.

slides.label: Chatbot vs agent
slides.source_text: Core · chatbot vs agent A chatbot answers. An agent acts. Chatbot — the one you know You ask → it tells you what to do → you open the files, run the commands, paste the errors back… and repeat. Agent You ask → it does the work itself — reads the files, runs the commands, checks the result → you review at the end. The model proposes actions. The harness executes permitted tools. Together, repeating this process, they form an agent.

slides.label: Model in the cloud
slides.source_text: Harness · what runs where Model in the cloud, harness on your machine YOU you talk → chat AGENT = harness + model, in a loop YOUR MACHINE (local) CLAUDE CODE the harness your files ▸ terminal runs actions CLOUD MODEL Claude model stateless — no memory sends context → ← next action You talk to the agent. Claude Code is the harness — it runs locally with your files & terminal, and loops with the model in the cloud (which stays stateless). The agent isn't a separate thing — it's that loop.

slides.label: No memory in practice
slides.source_text: Model · example "No memory" in practice There's no "conversation" on the model's side. Each call hands it the whole history as one flat list: # What the model is handed on turn 3 — the WHOLE chat, again: you said: "My name is David." it replied: "Nice to meet you, David." you now ask: "What's my name?" ← answerable only because line 1 was re-sent Delete the first line and the model can't answer. The "memory" lives in the request — not the model.

slides.label: The agent loop
slides.source_text: Agent · the loop An agent is a loop Propose: the model chooses the next action. Run: the harness executes it under the configured permissions. Observe: the result returns as context for the next step. Check: stop when the task is verified, or ask when blocked. In a live run or a finished transcript, point to one tool call and its result. That is one lap of the loop.

slides.label: Thinking
slides.source_text: Thinking · how it works The model thinks before it answers PROMPT ILLUSTRATIVE REASONING • recall the VAT rule (21%) • 100 × 1.21 = 121 • so the test expects the tax added (these reasoning tokens cost money too) ANSWER Reasoning gives the model room to work through intermediate steps before answering or acting. More effort can help a difficult diagnosis; it also takes more time and tokens. For the invoice task, verify the VAT rule and run the test. A plausible explanation alone is not evidence. Visible thinking may be a summary. Judge the result and the checks, not how convincing the narration sounds.

slides.source_text: Context · what it is Context = the model's short-term memory Context contains the instructions, conversation and tool results supplied for this call. The context window is the maximum capacity. Its size depends on the model and configuration. Supply the relevant test and invoice code. An unread file cannot guide the model through this request. slides.label: Context quality
slides.source_text: Context More context is not always more useful Useful context The failing test, the VAT rule and the code path that computes the total. Distracting context Old tasks, duplicate file dumps and unrelated logs that obscure those facts. Watch for ignored requirements, repeated work and missed evidence. There is no universal percentage at which quality fails.

Inspect the context display as a capacity indicator. Check behavior and results before deciding what to remove.

slides.label: Caching and compaction
slides.source_text: Context Cheaper reuse and shorter context Caching Reuses computed state for a matching prefix. It can reduce processing cost and latency; the content is still input. Compaction Replaces older material with a summary. It frees room, but details omitted from that summary may be lost. For the invoice task, preserve the VAT rule, failing test, attempted changes and verification command.

slides.label: Sub-agents
slides.source_text: Context · sub-agents Sub-agents keep the main context clean Delegate a focused investigation, such as finding every place invoice totals are calculated. The helper’s intermediate tool output stays in its own working context. Ask for a concise result with evidence. A fresh subagent needs a self-contained task. A conversation fork can inherit the existing history.

slides.label: Permissions
slides.source_text: Permissions Decide what the agent may touch Scope the work Allow the project files and test commands needed for the task. Keep approval points Ask before destructive actions, access changes or publishing outside the task. Contain mistakes For unattended experiments, restrict filesystem, network and credentials in an actual sandbox. A separate folder or Git branch protects neither credentials nor the rest of the machine. Check the configured boundary.

slides.label: Project rules
slides.source_text: Project knowledge Teach it the rules it cannot infer # CLAUDE.md — invoice project - Run invoice checks with: python -m unittest - VAT rates come from the order record. - Do not replace the tests to make a fix pass. - Ask before changing the stored invoice schema. Keep standing rules short. Use the instruction-file convention supported by your harness, such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

slides.label: MCP
slides.source_text: Reaching out · MCP MCP = "USB-C for agents" without MCP — N×M glue with MCP — connect once MCP MCP standardizes how a supported client discovers and calls tools exposed by a server. Example: read the issue describing the invoice bug, then propose an update with verification evidence. Each integration still needs compatible support, authentication and scoped permissions.
